newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain arrests E.Guinea ex-minister in drugs swoop.
newsitem.headline: Spain arrests E.Guinea ex-minister in drugs swoop.

text.p: Spanish police said on Wednesday they had detained Equatorial Guinea's former minister of information, Santos Pascual, in an anti-drug operation in which 22 people were arrested.

Pascual, who left his post on June 26, is a son-in-law of Equatorial Guinea's President Teodoro Obiang. He was arrested on July 6 at Madrid's Barajas airport carrying a suitcase containing 15 kg (34 lbs) of heroin, police said.

The arrests were part of an operation in which Spanish police worked closely with the government of the former Spanish colony to break up two international drug organisations dedicated to heroin trafficking from Pakistan.
The two groups were interconnected and encompassed people from Turkey, Iran, Spain and Equatorial Guinea, who tried to pass themselves off as diplomats, police said in a statement.
Police seized Equatorial Guinea government papers and documentation in the operation, along with the official seal from the Security Office of the tiny west African country.
The papers included blank passports and other identity documents, along with blank letterhead from various official organisations in Equatorial Guinea.
Police began the investigation to find out who was behind an increase in the heroin supply in Madrid.
Pascual was arrested after making a trip to Pakistan where, police said, he made contact with known Iranian drug traffickers involved in heroin distribution in Spain.
